function: MIMO-ODDM signal detection: a spatial-based GAN (AMFG generator, SAMD discriminator) recovers transmitted delay-Doppler symbols from received signals, with transfer-learning updating (TAU) (pp. 1-2, 5).
system: MIMO-ODDM, 3x3 antennas with half-wavelength ULA, 4QAM, 3.5 GHz carrier, 300 km/h, 8 paths, N=64, M=128; no RIS (pp. 9-10, Table I).
method: Spatial-based GAN (attention generator with six-directional LSTM, attention discriminator), supervised offline training with L1 plus adversarial loss; transfer-learning update (TAU) fine-tunes one block (pp. 5-9).
data_channel: Simulated 3GPP TDL-C channel (ref. [35]), random delay and Doppler indices, 8 paths; labelled dataset of 10^6 samples (15625 ODDM symbols), 60/40 train/test split (pp. 9-10).
test_conditions: Train on 60% of the dataset, test on 40% (10 rounds); new environments (similarity score) tested after TAU adaptation with 128 ODDM symbols (pp. 9-12).
baselines: Non-learned EDD [12] and MPMRC [13] (perfect and imperfect CSI); learned 2D-CNN [15], RC [17], symbol-DNN [34]; ablations without AMFG, SAM, TAU; full retraining (pp. 10-12).
metrics: BER versus SNR, number of paths, antennas, and speed; computational-complexity order; training loss convergence iterations; similarity score for TAU (pp. 10-12).
complexity: Table II gives the order O(8N_R^2N^2M^2+4MNN_R+4M^2N^2N_TN_R) for SG-ODDM versus baselines, training included; TAU converges in about 250 iterations (pp. 10, 12).
q1_support: p. 9: "the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) tapped delay line-C (TDL-C) model [35], to build up the MIMO-ODDM system".
q2_support: p. 12: "considerably outperforms the scenario without TAU in terms of BER performance, across a range of similarity scores"; p. 9: "TAU focuses on fine-tuning a specific part of SG-ODDM rather than retraining the entire model".
q3_support: p. 10: "other state-of-the-art non-DL and DL methods, i.e., EDD [12], MPMRC [13], 2D-CNN [15], RC [17] and symbol-DNN [34]"; "the proposed SG-ODDM performs best among all the detection methods in terms of BER performance".
q4_support: p. 10: "We further validate the computational complexity" ... "as illustrated in Table II"; Table II gives the order of the proposed SG-ODDM, O(8N_R^2 N^2 M^2 + 4MNN_R + 4M^2 N^2 N_T N_R).
q5_support: p. 5: "we generate a training dataset by acquiring the delay-Doppler-spatial (DDS) domain representations of the received ODDM signals". Data come from the authors' own simulation; the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public dataset.
notes: Area 4 rather than 1: ODDM is a delay-Doppler multicarrier scheme for high mobility (300-500 km/h) that the paper presents next to OTFS (p. 1); reviewer to confirm. q1 rests on the 3GPP TDL-C model cited from TS 38.104 [35], not TR 38.901 by name, and delay and Doppler indices are drawn at random (p. 9); reviewer to confirm. q2 rests on the TAU adaptation to new environments (Fig. 12); the path, antenna and speed sweeps (Figs. 7-9) do not say whether the model is retrained.
